title: S&P Global Investment Manager Index (Sep 2026) — 10:00 ET, the only buy-side risk-appetite survey on this calendar, released on FOMC day one
source: EST: read verbatim off S&P Global's own calendar listing, pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Release/ReleaseDates?language=en, re-fetched direct by this lane 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 23,858 bytes): 'September 15 | 14:00 UTC | S&P Global Investment Manager Index'. 14:00 UTC is 10:00 ET under EDT. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BY A DATE RULE DERIVED FROM THREE PRIMARY RELEASES, not by trusting the listing: S&P Global's press-release index (HTTP 200, 92,883 bytes) plus three IMI PDFs fetched direct this session give release dates 2026-01-13 (masthead 'Embargoed until 1000 EST (1500 UTC) 13 January 2026', data collected January 5-8), 2026-05-12 ('1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 12 May 2026', collected May 5-7) and 2026-08-11 ('1000 EDT (1400 UTC) 11 August 2026', collected August 1-7). All three are the Tuesday eight days after that month's first Monday; the same rule applied to September 2026 (first Monday 2026-09-07) yields 2026-09-15 exactly, which is why this edition is a THIRD Tuesday where the others were seconds. Filed estimate on the same standing schema gap the S&P Global PMI entries name — market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix for a private survey compiler — and because this lane does not self-confirm. The date is not in doubt; the label is about the taxonomy.
notes: The calendar's only BUY-SIDE forward-looking risk-appetite series. Researched 2026-09-09; canonical file written then from the one proposal that existed (from-sp-global-manufacturing-pmi-2026-10-01), which is now inert. That proposal made two claims and this lane tested both. (1) 'a class this calendar tracks nothing of' — REFINED, not confirmed: 44 tracked titles are surveys, but every one polls an economic actor about its own business or household (Conference Board, UMich, NAHB, Empire/Philly/Dallas, Tankan) or the credit plumbing (SLOOS, SCOOS-2026-09-24 on dealer financing terms). None asks an asset manager what it intends to do with US equities in the next 30 days. The narrow claim survives; the broad one does not. (2) 'its date makes it sharper than its impact tier suggests' — SPLIT. On the tape: refuted twice, by the consumer-confidence chain's exhaustive FOMC-day-one nulls and by this lane's own reading of the one verified IMI release day, 2026-08-11, whose 10:00-10:15 ET window ranked below its own median on 4 of 5 instruments (SPY p7, IWM p12, ^TNX exactly 0.000%) on a day this calendar tracks nothing else. On the information: SUPPORTED and sharpened — the date rule puts this edition's field window in the week of 09-07, making it the first 2026 edition whose panel answered AFTER the month's jobs report (August's own PDF says its panel answered 'before the August jobs report'). NOT A TRADE: symbols is empty, no macro-keyed house playbook, no published consensus exists for a sentiment survey, and the date is estimate. Read it on 09-16 morning as a prior on how positioned the panel already was; attribute nothing on 09-15.
